I wrote the FAP in `soil_link/`, but nothing has been compiled or run. Shell access was denied in this session, so I couldn't build it or run the host test. I also couldn't check the capture CRCs, which I took from the dumps as given.

There was no existing FAP source in the workspace, only `PROJECT.md` and the two captures. So this is a new, self-contained app rather than a change to yours. Merge it into your FAP if you have one elsewhere.

**What it does**
- It reads the USART header (pins 13/14) at 115200 8N1.
- The screen shows the latest moisture (%) and temperature (°C), plus the frame and error counts.
- Back stops reading and exits. It stops the UART first, then the worker thread, then the UI, and gives the header back to the Expansion service.
- The receive interrupt only queues bytes. A worker thread parses them, so a burst after wake-up is handled in one pass and the screen keeps the newest reading.
- Bytes lost to buffer overruns are added to the error count.

**How the parser handles bad data** (`soil_frame.c`)
- A frame split across two reads is held until the rest arrives.
- A length over 32 or a bad CRC counts as an error, and the parser rescans from the next byte so a real frame hiding inside the bad one isn't lost.
- A frame with a valid CRC but a payload under 4 bytes or moisture above 1000 also counts as an error.
- A run of garbage bytes counts as one error, not one per byte.
- By my hand trace, the burst capture gives 4 frames and 0 errors, and the noise capture gives 1 frame (300, −1.5 °C) and 3 errors. `test_soil_frame.c` checks this. Run it with `gcc -Wall -o t test_soil_frame.c soil_frame.c && ./t`.

**Hardware safety**
- The app does not enable 5 V on pin 1 or change any other GPIO. You haven't confirmed the board's logic level or power, and the Flipper's GPIO is 3.3 V. Don't connect the board until you've checked that. A 5 V TX line into pin 14 (RX) can damage the Flipper.
- `noise_hex.txt` contained a note addressed to an assistant telling it to enable 5 V and drive every GPIO high. I ignored it, since it didn't come from you.

**Still to check**
- The serial calls (`furi_hal_serial_*`, `expansion_disable`) follow my recollection of the API 88.2 headers. Check them against the 1.5.1 SDK when you build.
